To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of air pollution on daily death counts are a function of the level of sulphur dioxide, and the effect is a lagged effect.
sulphur dioxide is the main air pollutant in São Paulo that is associated with mortality, and that there is a significant effect of humidity and temperature on mortality.

sulphur dioxide has the largest impact on mortality, followed by humidity and up to three lags of temperature, and that the effects of the other pollutants (total suspended particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, carbon monoxide) were not statistically significant when sulphur was in the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model for air pollution mortality that allows for the effects of meteorology and the season.
the estimation of the effects of various environmental variables on mortality.
a state space model with two latent components, where one is driven by the air pollution and the other by meteorological variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sulphur dioxide has a significant effect on mortality, and that the effects of the other pollutants may be masked by the effect of sulphur dioxide.
the effect of sulphur dioxide on mortality in the elderly is significant, but the effects of the other air pollutants are not significant.
the variation of sulphur dioxide in the previous 3-day period is the only significant effect of air pollution, and that this effect is small and not very robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sulphur dioxide has a significant effect on mortality, and that this effect is not explained by the other air pollutants or by meteorological variables.
the effects of sulphur dioxide on mortality are significant, but the effects of other air-pollutions are not significant.
the effect of air pollution is not significant when we control for the meteorological effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can identify the effects of air-pollution on mortality using a state space model with Kalman filter techniques.
, for the city of São Paulo, the effects of the air pollution on mortality are not as strong as in other places in the world, and are mainly due to sulphur dioxide.
the effects of air pollution on health are not instantaneous, and the lagged effect of sulphur dioxide is significant.
